title: How to use Pleat Sewing tool?
content:
I've watched several YouTube videos, including CLO official ones, and I am still missing some key insight into how to use the Pleat Sewing tool.

The Pleats tool does work - if I first do Free Sewing or Segment Sewing, and then use the Pleats tool, that goes fine:

![f8777521af1e4d28bc2a0dc600dd7983](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/18aa59af53e84b3bb364b5e5f57627b2/images/f8777521af1e4d28bc2a0dc600dd7983Screenshot%202025-09-18%20at%202.11.05%E2%80%AFpm.png)

However, if I do not do Free Sewing or Segment Sewing first, and try to do Free Sewing after using Pleats tool:

![df02fbb4e1a84355b620ea787b91fc94](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/18aa59af53e84b3bb364b5e5f57627b2/images/df02fbb4e1a84355b620ea787b91fc94Screenshot%202025-09-18%20at%202.12.19%E2%80%AFpm.png)

I have also tried many times to use Internal lines (extended and added points) and then Pleats Fold, and then Pleats Sewing, but there I also do not understand how to use Pleats Sewing correctly. I've tried making Internal lines and points on the 'non pleated' pattern piece too, without success for Pleats Sewing.

My question is:

  * How to use Pleats Sewing?

    * After using Pleats, if I had to remove the sewing and want to redo it; or

    * After making Internal lines and Pleat Folds

### Community Post Comments:


Comment 2: I am making some progress here myself.I have found:The Pleats Folding is just setting the Fold Strength and Fold Angle on the Internal Line. You can set this yourself too, and change it. The colour of the line is from the Fold Angle. The Pleats Sewing is sewing the first segment to the other piece, then the first segment to the second, and the second to the third. And then repeats. You need to NOT use the tool all the way to the 'final' segment point yourself, otherwise if you put mouse over that final one, it'll think you're starting a new sequence of 3.If you want any sewing before or after the pleats, do that yourself seperately. This means if you undo the sewing the Pleats tool makes, you can't actually repeat it using Pleats Sewing, unless you add in some segment points on the other pattern piece.
Reply 1: I have noticed the Pleats Sewing tool is a bit like Free Sewing tool, so on the unpleated pattern piece, you don't need to start/stop at a segment point. So strictly speaking, points do not need adding. So it IS possible to re-sew what Pleats does, with Pleats Sewing tool.
content_description: This web page aims to provide clear guidance and troubleshooting tips for effectively using the Pleat Sewing tool in CLO, addressing common challenges and best practices.

title: Material Type Not Working
content:
Hello CLO Team,

Since the latest update, the _Material Type_ function in CLO 3D does not work properly. Knitwear and Denim cannot be applied, and sometimes other material types also fail. I already tried reinstalling CLO 3D, but the issue continues.

I am working on a **MacBook Pro M3 Max** , so this may be related to compatibility with the new Apple chips. This problem makes it very difficult to work, while my subscription keeps running. Please advise if this is a known bug or provide a solution.

Thank you,

Vida![3091e63cda9a4647b72143b1615b6ef5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/2ddd15b55c584174a30a762b35e93585/images/3091e63cda9a4647b72143b1615b6ef5Screenshot%202025-09-11%20at%2014.23.34.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi Ariel,Thanks for your tips! I’m working on a MacBook Pro M3 Max, so memory doesn’t seem to be the issue. I’ve noticed that the problem can appear when resizing a default avatar in Avatar Editor, or sometimes when using purchased hair. Technically I don’t understand why, but at least now I know where the problem comes from.Best regards,Vida❤️
Reply 1: Hi VidaThis issue often occurs when using Fur, Knitwear, or a Displacement Map.These features generate an enormous number of polygons to increase the mesh detail, which creates a load equivalent to loading dozens of garments in the 3D window. As a result, even the latest devices can run out of memory. If the purchased hair has a higher polygon count or texture resolution than the default hair, it may also contribute to reaching the memory limit.I recommend enabling 'Frustum Culling' and 'LOD' in the rendering properties, and then performing a Final Render. 'Frustum Culling' removes polygons outside the camera's view when rendering starts, while 'LOD' reduces the polygon count for objects farther from the camera. Both features are useful for optimizing memory.
Reply 2: You are absolutely right . I truly value your professional insight .Those were my first thoughts too, but unfortunately it didn’t solve the issue. Nothing shows up in render… and sometimes I even get funny/scary glitches like just eyeballs and teeth instead of the avatar 😂👻 Thank you again for sharing your expertise.🙏🏻

Comment 2: Dear Ariel,After resolving the previous material issues, I am now experiencing another issue. Knitwear garments display correctly in the 3D window, but they disappear in the render window. I have already ensured that Show Knitwear is turned on and that the garments are fully simulated, but the problem persists.I am using a MacBook Pro M3 Max with the latest CLO 3D update. This issue prevents me from properly rendering my knit designs. Please advise if this is a known bug or provide guidance on how to fix it.Thank you very much for your support.
Reply 1: First, I love this knit pattern here! ❤️Second, For this issue it could be a few different things. But most often it is due to the computer now having enough memory/RAM to complete the render. I would try a few of the below things first to lighten the the file while rendering. But if these do not help please send the file and computer specs (about this mac) directly to the CLO contact us page -Change Noise threshold from 0.025 to 0.050 (default). Also for Noise I usually do not recommend going below 0.030 in future-For your render Engine. I cannot see which version you have selected. So possibly try to switch to the other option.One thing that can also sometimes help (especially with heavy files) is restarting CLO. Or if you have not turned your computer off in awhile restarting your computer

Comment 3: Hi Vida. We are sorry to hear you are having issues. For Knitwear you do need to make sure that Show knitwear is Turned On in the 3D vertical Toggle. You will then see the changes made in the 3D windowFor Denim you will still need to apply a fabric first (not the default fabric). A Denim, twill, or other likely woven material. Once you have a fabric with visual properties to work with you can change the Type to Denim and adjust the different settings
Reply 1: Hi Ariel,Thank you so much for your quick and very clear reply😍 — I really appreciate it! 🙏 Turning on Show Knitwear completely solved the issue for me. Regarding Denim, I still need to try a few different fabric properties to get it just right, but I’m totally happy now. I trust your guidance and feel confident working in CLO 3D again.Your support was extremely helpful.❤️🙏🏻Vida
Reply 2: You are welcome and so glad to hear that!!!! ❤️❤️❤️
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to address and seek solutions for compatibility issues with the _Material Type_ function in CLO 3D on MacBook Pro M3 Max, specifically regarding the application of Knitwear and Denim materials.

title: How to get output of different styles with different sizes same in clo3d.
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/b11a9f7978d44517bcbf7bba85bde782/images/f4d8b9d8aa3e455980e627fbd8bba55cScreenshot%202025-09-08%20151546.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202509/b11a9f7978d44517bcbf7bba85bde782/images/ef68796cae19418e829a1aaa1818d784Down%20hoodie_0.gif)I need help regarding 360 turntable rendering in Clo3D. I design multiple garments of different sizes (short and long), but in 360 turntable rendering I want to keep all of their sizes the same. I have tried everything, every setting is the same for every style, but still the longer jacket appears big and the short jacket appears small.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Make sure when recording the video/animation in CLO that the garments are placed on the same location. If you have hidden avatars make sure they are both standing at 000 (center of the 3D space) and are the same height.For the Camera Check the focal distance, Camera Field of View. and then for a turntable you are always starting at the same point (best to create a Custom view and use that for both projects).Or you can instead make a camera rotation and use the Animation mode to do this. It is a more advanced option, but will give you more control.Also keep in mind these are two very different garments. One is larger and oversized and the other is more tight fitting. So the Tight fitting one will naturally be smaller than the oversized one
content_description: This web page aims to provide guidance and solutions for achieving consistent 360 turntable rendering of garments in Clo3D, regardless of their varying sizes.
